newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers file bill to end Canada lumber quota.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers file bill to end Canada lumber quota.

text.p: A bill to end the U.S. quota on imported Canada lumber was unveiled Thursday by 20 members of the U.S. House (of Representatives).
Backers said the bill would result in lower housing prices and make it easier for Americans to buy a house.

Groups representing home builders, lumber dealers and retailers gave their support to the legislation. Daniel Pincus, president of the National Association of Home Builders, called the year-old quota "a mistake" that drove up lumber costs. "This is something the president needs to change."
Under an April 1996 agreement, up to 14.7 billion board feet of Canadian lumber can enter the United States duty-free each year. Taxes are assessed on shipments above that level.
Representative Jack Quinn, R-N.Y., said House leadership had not taken a position on his bill and a companion Senate bill was being sought.

The bill would change a trade law to say that Canadian lumber programs were not subject to U.S. countervailing duties. The change would allow Canada to back out of the lumber pact without running the risk of a countervailing duty suit.
NAHB staff workers said the bill would go to the Ways and Means Committee.
